stem:
Meena's school garden in Jaipur has four patches of soil. After rain, she wants to know through which patch water will seep down fastest. She reads that water seeps fastest through a material whose particles have wider, open and well-connected spaces between them.
The table describes the spaces between the particles in each patch.
Through which patch will water seep down fastest?

options.text: clay; very narrow spaces, poorly connected
fine sand; narrow spaces, moderately connected
coarse sand; medium spaces, fairly connected

teacher.key_rationale: Seepage is fastest where spaces between particles are widest and best connected; gravel has wide, well-connected pores, so water passes through it fastest. Clay (A) is the trap for students who think the finest, smoothest-looking material lets water through fastest.
